purpose: This medication is most commonly used to help prevent your body from rejecting a transplanted organ, such as a kidney, heart, or liver. It is also sometimes used to treat certain autoimmune conditions where your immune system is attacking your own body. It is almost always used together with other medications to keep your immune system in check.
how_it_works: Your immune system normally fights off things it sees as foreign, like germs — but after a transplant, it may also attack your new organ. Mycophenolate mofetil works by slowing down the production of certain white blood cells that lead that attack. By reducing the number of these cells, your body is less likely to reject the new organ or attack its own tissues.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, and loss of appetite. You may also notice feeling tired, headaches, or dizziness. Some people experience low blood counts, which can make you more prone to infections or feeling weak and fatigued.
warnings: Because this medication lowers your immune system, you are at a higher risk of getting serious infections, including some rare but dangerous ones. It also increases the risk of certain cancers, especially skin cancer, so avoid too much sun and use sunscreen regularly. This medication can cause serious birth defects and must NOT be taken during pregnancy — effective birth control is required. Never stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is usually 1,000 mg (1 gram) taken twice a day, but your doctor may adjust this based on your specific condition and how well you tolerate it. It is usually taken with or without food, but taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and try to take it at the same times each day.
